title: Keep up to N objective tasks in flight per mission, each on its own agent
prompt:
Read `assign_next`, `next_open` and `load_backlog` in crates/spawn-cli/src/objectives.rs; `Integrator::mission`, `Mission::ready`, `Mission::landing`, `enforce_budget` and `judge` in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs; `GATED` and `OBJECTIVE_MISSIONS` in crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs; `spawn_mission_configure`, `spawn_objective_assign`, `spawn_task_assign` and `spawn_task_may_continue` in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql; `Settings` in crates/spawn-cli/src/missions.rs; `orders()` and `collect_reports()` in crates/spawn-cli/src/deliver.rs; and docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3-10.4.

The problem. A gated objective mission has one worker, its resident (`objectives ->> 'resident'`). `assign_next` returns as soon as the mission has any open task, and `spawn_objective_assign` always assigns to the resident, whose next task the dispatcher holds until the last one lands. So one objective is in flight per mission, whatever the backlog. Supply PA (mission 6) did six objectives one after another, about 6 minutes each. Its next slice and Spawn's own 006-008 are independent of each other, so throughput is bounded by one agent per mission, not by the work.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks):
1. A worker limit N per objective mission, stored in its objectives as `"workers": N` and set by `spawn mission configure --id M ... --backlog <dir> --resident <name> --workers N` (and by `spawn mission add` with the same settings, which share `Settings`). Default 1: a mission configured without `--workers`, and every objectives jsonb already in the log, behaves exactly as today. `spawn_mission_configure` refuses a `workers` that is not an integer from 1 to 16, with a clear message. Update the usage text.
2. The integrator keeps up to N objective tasks of the mission in flight. A task is in flight from `task.assigned` until it is landed or cancelled (assigned, delivered, revise, reported, accepted, landing). Each pass may fill free slots with the lowest open objectives that have no task in flight. An open objective never has two tasks in flight. `spawn_objective_assign` checks both rules under the append lock (the objective already in flight, the mission at N) and raises otherwise, so a second integrator or a stale read cannot oversubscribe.
3. Each in-flight task has its own agent. The resident takes a task whenever it has none open. Every other task goes to a new per-task worker, created by the assignment the way `spawn_task_assign` creates an ephemeral one: kind `ephemeral`, agent `agent_worker_objective_<task>`, session `session_worker_objective_<task>`, the same brief, `created_by` `spawn-integrate`, the objective and its scenario recorded as for the resident's tasks. Why this and not a pool of N residents: a resident needs a human's approval (`spawn_resident_approve`), and a pool would mean N approvals and N long-lived sessions per mission. An ephemeral worker needs no approval, starts from the mission's source main as it is now, and is already stopped by the dispatcher once its gated task lands or is cancelled (`orders()`, `retire-task-<id>`), so cleanup needs nothing new. Its report reaches the supervisor's digest as any report does; add no new kind of digest item. The resident keeps its context, and the per-task workers keep none.
4. Landing stays one at a time and in gate order: one candidate judged per integrator pass, the lowest ready task first, and the compare-and-swap push of main as today. A task whose base is no longer main lands as the merge by main's merge rules (`landing_candidate`). When two in-flight objectives touch the same lines, the second is gated `conflict`, resolves the conflict and lands. A separate owner fix (branch `conflict-merge`) makes a `conflict` verdict merge main into the worker's workspace with markers, and merges main into the worker's branch at delivery. Assume that behaviour: do not build your own merge into workspaces, and do not change what `conflict` means.
5. Budgets (`--minutes`, `--tool-calls`) apply per task, from that task's delivery, as `enforce_budget` does now. The halt rules stay per mission: three gate rejections in a row across all the mission's tasks, whichever task they came from, halt it (`gate_rejections`, reset by an acceptance). A halted mission gets no new assignments, and its in-flight tasks are not judged until a human resumes it.
6. State the rule in docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.4 (the worker limit, who gets which task, at most one task per objective) and in the module comments of objectives.rs and integrate.rs (step 5 there says "with no open task").
Add unit tests: in objectives.rs, the choice of objectives for free slots (lowest open first, skipping objectives in flight, nothing at N, a recurring objective in flight not chosen twice); in crates/spawn-postgres/tests/, `spawn_objective_assign` refusing at N and refusing a second task for an objective in flight, the resident getting a task while it has none open and an `agent_worker_objective_<task>` otherwise, and `spawn_mission_configure` refusing workers 0 and 17.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/009.sh (read it). A real `spawn loop` (no model judge, no supervisor) runs every worker with a fake engine, `spawn integrate --once` passes land their work through a recording gate (SPAWN_GATE) that accepts every candidate, and the pusher publishes to local sources. Each objective's prompt names a file and its content (`BB:TASK <file> <word>`). The fake engine waits at a barrier until 3 tasks have reached their engines (or a hold runs out), then writes the file, and reports in a second turn once its checkpoint is pushed. (1) A mission configured with `--workers 3` and a backlog of 4 independent objectives, each a different file, with one approved resident: within 90 s, 3 objective tasks are delivered at once, on 3 distinct agents, exactly one of them the resident. Their delivered-to-reported intervals overlap. Never more than 3 of the mission's tasks are open at once, and never two for one objective. The fourth is assigned only after a landing. All 4 land, each once, and the source's main holds all four files. (2) A mission configured without `--workers`, with a backlog of 3: the tasks run one after another on its resident. Never two are open at once, each is assigned after the one before it landed and delivered after it reported. All 3 land on main. The conflict case of 4 is not in the scenario, because it needs the conflict-merge fix. It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
